pass_a_gloss:
Angels rouse all humanity through the sign of Lazarus, and nations are loosed like a foal and come to be ruled by their creator, then heaven and humans are at peace, and they cry out and say: 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, peace on earth and glory in the highest.' They put garments on the foal, which signify the grace given to them in the nations, and through it they mounted Jesus on them. Not only this, but also through their own virtues, as the evangelist means, saying: 'Others spread their garments on the road.' To this, their own virtues, which they yoked to grace, are praised, as the divine Paul clearly says: 'Having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we also have access by faith to this grace, in which we stand, and we boast in hope of the glory of God.' So far, the things of grace. 'Not only this, but also we boast in our tribulations, knowing that tribulation produces endurance, endurance produces proven character, and proven character produces hope; and hope does not disappoint, because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us.' The phrase 'on the earth they spread' means that their virtues were visibly and sensibly observed by the nations, as the apostle also says in another place.

As you saw and heard and received in me, do these things; but let us return to the preceding matter. The crowds preceding and following him cried out with praises and olive and palm branches, which signify the practical work of the outer man, and palm branches, which signify the spiritual and practical and pure work of the inner man. They cried out saying 'Hosanna in the highest'. In truth, all the crowds of the righteous and prophets and priests, who are those preceding and following, cry out and say with faith 'Hosanna to the son of David; blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest'. As the evangelist says, 'All this happened that the word spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying 'Tell the daughter of Zion'. The prophet says 'I desired to see and hear, not I alone but also many prophets and righteous ones'. But also to those finding and being disciples, seeing and hearing the king of Zion, I say that they might say and proclaim 'Tell the daughter of Zion; behold your king comes to you, righteous and saving, saving from the slavery of the enemy those believing in him'.

He is gentle and mounted on a donkey, a colt, the son of a beast of burden, that is, humble and in his humility destroying the chariots of the kingdom of Ephraim, that is, of the devil who ruled over Israel and the nations, and he destroyed also the kingdom of the people of the Jews, and the anointing and the kingdom of the Jews came until Christ and ceased, and he says 'and a horse' from Jerusalem, that is, all the pride of their authority, through his humble donkey, and the patriarch Jacob, blessing Judah and showing the blessing towards his fathers Abraham and Isaac, which is Christ, says 'tying his donkey to a vine', for he tied the unclean nations to the vine that came from Egypt, which filled the whole earth with the teaching of its prophets and righteous ones, and the donkey is unclean in the law, just like the nations, and he tied his donkey to a vine, why, so that they may receive from it the law and the prophets and the knowledge of God in them, that is, Christ, who is the blessing of the nations and their purification, and he says 'and to the vine, the donkey of his she-donkey', the vine, that is, the shoot that came from the vine, which is Christ, who sprouted from the vine of the synagogue that came from Egypt, as Jacob himself says to him, 'from a shoot'
pass_b_english: As angels rouse all humanity through the sign of Lazarus, and heaven and humanity are at peace, and they cry out in unison, saying: 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, peace on earth and glory in the highest' (Matthew 21:9).
They put garments on the foal, which signifies the grace given to the nations, and through this grace they mounted Jesus upon it, and by their own virtues (καὶ διὰ τὰς ἰδίας ἀρετάς).
Additionally, they are praised for their own virtues, which they have yoked to grace, as is evident when others spread their garments on the road (Matthew 21:8).

According to the divine Paul, having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we also have access by faith to this grace, in which we stand, and we boast in hope of the glory of God (Romans 5:1-2).

Furthermore, we boast in our tribulations, knowing that tribulation produces endurance, and endurance produces proven character, and proven character produces hope, and this hope does not disappoint, because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us (Romans 5:3-5).

The crowds that preceded and followed him cried out with praises and olive and palm branches, which signify the practical work of the outer man, and palm branches, which signify the spiritual and practical and pure work of the inner man, and they cried out saying: 'Hosanna in the highest' (Matthew 21:9).

In truth, all the crowds of the righteous and prophets and priests, who are those preceding and following, cry out and say with faith: 'Hosanna to the son of David; blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest' (Matthew 21:9).

As the evangelist says, all this happened that the word spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying 'Tell the daughter of Zion' (Matthew 21:5); the prophet says that he desired to see and hear, not he alone but also many prophets and righteous ones.

The prophet says to tell the daughter of Zion that her king is coming to her, and he says 'he is coming to you', that is, to be yours and to dwell in you, righteous and saving, saving from the slavery of the enemy those who believe in him (Matthew 21:5, Zechariah 9:9).

He is gentle and mounted on a donkey, a colt, the son of a beast of burden, and in his humility, he destroys the chariots of the kingdom of Ephraim, which represents the devil's rule over Israel and the nations; until Christ came, the anointing and the kingdom of the Jews came and ceased.
Through his humble donkey, the pride of their authority is destroyed, which is from Jerusalem.

The patriarch Jacob blesses Judah and shows that the blessing is directed towards his fathers Abraham and Isaac, which ultimately points to Christ; Jacob says that he ties his donkey to a vine, so that the unclean nations may receive from it the law and the prophets, and ultimately receive Christ, who is the blessing of the nations and their purification.

Jacob also says that the donkey is tied to the vine, which is a symbol of Christ, who sprouted from the vine of the synagogue that came from Egypt, as indicated by the phrase 'from a shoot' (Genesis 49:11).
